He is accused of orchestrating “one of the biggest financial frauds in American history” [3], with the SEC alleging FTX was a fraud “from the start” and that there was a “multi-billion-dollar deficiency caused by his own misappropriation of customer funds” [5][8]. The prosecution alleged he directed the misappropriation of $14 billion from customers to repay debts to lenders, as testified by Alameda’s former CEO Caroline Ellison, who said she took that amount under SBF’s instruction [4]. He was found guilty on seven counts including wire fraud [5].
